Acer K202HQL bd 20” (19.5" viewable) HD+ (1600 x 900) Monitor (DVI & VGA Ports) This monitor is a disappointment right out of the box. The instructions tell you how to connect the monitor arm to the base but not how to connect the monitor arm to the monitor (oops!). Once I figured that out, I connected the monitor using a spare HDMI cable I had around (they only give you a VGA to VGA cable). The picture quality, even after adjusting brightness, color, warmth, etc. is mediocre. It's dim and a little on the blurry side. Not pleasant to look at.

The base is a bit wobbly and I wouldn't trust this to stay upright if you have a child or large cat around!

The resolution, at 1366x768, makes everything zoomed way in if you're using this with a MacBook Air. As an example, if I click on the Apple menu, the height of the open menu takes up almost half the screen.

I'd be thrilled if I got this at a garage sale for $25 but for $70 on Amazon, it's too expensive for how poor quality it is.
text_fidelity_b: Acer K202HQL bd 20” (19.5" viewable) HD+ (1600 x 900) Monitor (DVI & VGA Ports)

text_fidelity_a:
HP Wireless Elite Keyboard v2 ...if you don't have a wrist rest or pad already, I highly recommend that you get one at the same time you get this keyboard. I was introduced to the chiclet- or scissor-style keyboard because of using one at work (using an Apple wired keyboard with an Intel Mac), and I have to say that I prefer it in every way to the more traditional keyboards. It is much quieter, and, for me, the feedback is pleasant. One thing I did not take into account, though, is that I had a wrist rest at work. So when I got this keyboard for home use and started using it, I loved it immediately--until the day I used it for hours on end. Then--ouch! My wrists began to ache.

Overall, this is a great keyboard. It connected to my computer without a problem, and the only lag in keystrokes I have experienced has been when the computer had just been "awakened" from sleep mode. For reasons I will not go into here, I am using this keyboard with a laptop: the laptop keyboard's lights indicate whether or not I have Caps Lock or Num Lock engaged on the wireless keyboard. I understand that won't help people using this keyboard with a desktop computer, but thought I'd put it out there anyway.

My conclusion: if you're a fan of the scissor-style keyboard and you have or are willing to invest in a wrist rest, you will enjoy this keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: HP Wireless Elite Keyboard v2

(72 x 108 inch) Pure White Backdrop Screen, 100% Pure Seamless Background, High Density 150 GSM Fabric with Elastic String Clips for Photo Video Streaming Studio, JSAG103 Even though I am a photographer, I didn't buy these for photography backdrops. I bought them to use as curtains for my master bedroom and, for that, they are perfect!

They are very lightweight, almost obliquely translucent at times, and they aren't stitched super well (there are little threads you'll need to clip), but otherwise, they are PERFECT. They steam VERY easily when hung (a problem with a lot of thicker backdrops), are super soft and gorgeous when hung.

The only other problem I have with them is that the last one of five I have ordered came stained in several areas--and it's stained with something grey-tan that neither washes or even bleaches out. So...it's going back.

Still, all in all, these are SUCH a find for the price! If I decide to get more to use as a photo backdrop, I'd get two and layer them, because just one will likely show whatever is behind it, and they would also easily show tension if you try to place anything like a chair or other prop on them.

text_fidelity_a:
Crucial X6 4TB Portable SSD - Up to 800MB/s - PC and Mac - USB 3.2 USB-C External Solid State Drive - CT4000X6SSD9 Crucial is one of the first names that comes to mind when I have needed reliable RAM for my systems in the past. I have a Crucial 500MB SSD in one of my systems and it has served me well over the years so I was interested in this SSD as a back-up option for pictures and data. It has proven to be a fine solution for my needs.

Right up front – yes, it works with Linux right out of the box. I plugged it into my Peppermint Linux system and the kernel immediately recognized the drive and made it available. It was on me to mount the drive, but this was a simple matter and I was able to access the file system and see drive statistics. Obviously it works with Windows so I won’t go into that.

This is a physically small device, slightly less than half the size of a cell phone (iPhone 6s is what I used for comparison). It will easily fit inside the change pocket in my jeans and can tuck just about anywhere. This is a double-edged sword. On one hand it is convenient to have something this small and easy to store, but it is also easy to misplace or even lose. If this stays in your laptop bag or briefcase it should be secure, but if you are in a habit of keeping things in your pockets instead be cautious.

Transfer speeds are good. I have not done benchmarks on this drive but I copied thousands of pictures (average size about 8mb per file, some more and some less) and it was significantly faster than the USB drive I have been using for a while and faster than many of the thumb drives I have been using for backups. I have no complaints.

This is a small and fast drive that just works. It works with Linux which for me is important, and it is small enough to tuck in my camera bag for making backups in the field.
text_fidelity_b: Crucial X6 4TB Portable SSD - Up to 800MB/s - PC and Mac - USB 3.2 USB-C External Solid State Drive - CT4000X6SSD9

For wiring that was on the same breaker box (but far enough away that wifi from the router was poor, around -70 dBm), I saw excellent speeds of 50+Mbps over wifi connected to the extender both up and down. I have Fios that goes up to 75-80 Mbps. For wiring that was on the 2nd box (so it had to go over a longer circuit to get to the adapter box wired to my router), speeds were a bit slower, around 30 Mpbs, but plenty fast as far as I'm concerned. I'm buying a 2nd extender so that I can have one extender at each end of my house. Oh, and copying my ssid/password/channel to the extender was a cinch. I found that I had to turn wifi off and back on again to get my device to connect to the nearest adapter, otherwise it was a piece of cake.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link Powerline WiFi Extender - Powerline Adapter with WiFi, WiFi Booster, Plug & Play, Power Saving, Ethernet over Power, Expand both Wired and WiFi Connections, AV600 (TL-WPA4220 KIT)

text_fidelity_a:
Homvare Hard Shell Case for Over The Ear Headphones with Full Protection fits Beats Studio, Solo 3, Sony, Bose QC, JBL, Sennheiser, Skullcandy, mPow, Audio Technica, Cowin, JVC, Panasonic I wanted a simple hardshell case to attach a carabiner to and sling my noise-canceling headphones off my backpack. This did the job. It was fine, I was pleased.

Then I came back from a December trip to Helsinki and somewhere between baggage claim at DFW and my front door, the case - with my beloved headphones, a battery bank, and my Apple rapid charge block - vanished.

I was heartbroken. I filed reports. I checked with my Lyft driver. I went through my backpack and suitcase over and over and over again. I poked the bushes around my apartment building. Nothing.

Fast forward four months to today. I took the trash out and as I came back up the stairs, I saw something dark colored under the feral cat shelter on my patio. In all these months I’d never noticed it. But when I lifted the shelter, there it was. Filthy, scratched up, covered in pollen - my headphone case. I believe I knocked it under there while I was looking for my house keys.

In the last four months the DFW area has seen torrential downpours, freezing sleet, and even snowdrifts. My porch often catches the brunt of these storms. And yet when I zipped the case open, my headphones and battery bank and charging block were perfectly fine. Not so much as a dust mote on them. Everything was still fully charged and absolutely totally functional. As if they hadn’t just spent four months outdoors in Texas’ wacky winter weather under a cat hutch. Completely perfect.

And the case may be fine externally as well once I take some Clorox wipes to it.

Anyway. Good case, STUPENDOUS dang value for the cost.
text_fidelity_b: Homvare Hard Shell Case for Over The Ear Headphones with Full Protection fits Beats Studio, Solo 3, Sony, Bose QC, JBL, Sennheiser, Skullcandy, mPow, Audio Technica, Cowin, JVC, Panasonic

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I bought this as a graduation present for my nephew and, of course, had to try it out for a while just to make sure it was "in proper functioning order." (OK, so I like toys even more than the kids do).

Very nice system! It's a nice improvement from earlier Nuvi's I've used. Love the improved software, especially the full-time next-turn indicator (long a favorite feature of mine on Magellan units). The screen layout is attractive and easy to use, even for those of us with less than perfect eyesight.

While I personally like the Magellan systems better for my own use, I picked this for the nephew for a couple of reasons. First, it has features such as the ability to download Google maps directions. Not something I would use, but a nice feature for those who would use it. Second, it has the ability to display the speed limit. While it won't prevent speeding, at least it's a reminder for a younger driver to keep it slow.

I found the routing engine to be top-notch. Every GPS does that a bit different, but every route I planned on it was plotted out in a logical manner. It's a bit slower to detect off-route conditions and re-route compared with Magellans, but certainly does it at an acceptable speed. Boot up and acquitiion time is very good, as it the overall build quality and form factor.

A good option to pick up is a bean bag mount such as a NavMat. Makes it far easier to hide the GPS without any trace to tip off potential theves.

Most important, it has Garmin support - they are far better than Magellan, and can be used as a resource for someone who is using their first GPS. I was sorry to have to hand it back over the the nephew, but he's thrilled with it!
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Gator Cases 28" Creative Pro Bag for Video Camera Systems with Wheels & Pull Handle (GCPRVCAM28W) Let me start off by saying I work in freelance video and I love how much I can fit inside this case! I've been using a Pelican 1510 as my go-to travel carrier, so that's mostly what I'm comparing this to. For starters, this is a longer case so in addition to my cameras, lenses, batteries and other accessories, it has a long open sleeve that can even fit a light stand or small tripod! For extra versatility, the whole interior can actually be pulled out (it has its own handle straps if you want to use it as its own carrier), which then frees up the ample storage space inside the case as a separate giant unit (see pictures to illustrate). There are also plenty of pockets on the inside, as well as the outside and front of the case. Of course, for a case this size there is the requisite wheels and carrying handle.
The only things I like better about my Pelican case, however, are the toughness and waterproofing. This bag comes with a rain cover which you can keep inside the case, however I don't like the idea of having to carry around a cover inside the bag, then take it out and put it on if it starts raining. The Pelican cases are air tight by simply closing them, no rain cover needed. The Pelican cases also are tough enough that they can be stacked under other equipment, thrown into a corner, sat on, stood on, etc, and 99% of the time come out unscathed. That's more than I can say for this bag. I bring this bag on gigs that I'm not worried about those things happening, because I can fit what I normally take in 3 separate bags into just this one. You could get a Pelican style case in this size, however it would cost quite a bit more than the asking price of this one. I think for the price this is a great tool to keep your stuff organized and ready to go whenever you are!

However, the customer service is beyond satisfactory. I am deeply pleased. When it arrived broken, within 2 days I received a new one (I did send photos of the broken one). I did find out something tremendous, though. The broken screen held together safely. I was cracked and had fan-like cracks from edge to edge, but it didn't fall apart. It was smooth to the touch, so if for any reason your screen gets cracked on your device, don't worry about it scratching the screen. It won't.

Never did. But I did with the first try with this one. Just be careful to clean your screen really well under a bright light so you can see all the particles and spots. Lay the glass screen on the end, and push down (fairly hard) with the enclosed triangular plastic piece as you gently lower the glass screen onto your device's screen. If you do it slowly, you won't have any bubbles. If you see a piece of dirt that you missed, then lift the corner gently and dab the glass screen with the blue sticky paper enclosed. That keeps your fingerprints from the sticky side of the glass screen. Dab your device's screen with the blue sticky paper to be sure you removed all the dirt. Slide the triangular plastic piece over the indentation and it should give you a perfect seal over the device's screen.

It's beautiful.

Air Duster & Vacuum 2-in-1, Cordless Electric Compressed Air Blower for Computer Keyboard Cleaning Replaces Canned Air Spray, Portable Handheld Electronics Car Computer Duster, Powerful 77000RPM Motor I do a lot of work on sewing machines and electronics that need to be sprayed with air often. I was having a hard time with canned air working right or stopping working before it was gone. Then I saw this. I am never going back!

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a combo vacuum/blower. It has a clear blue top on it for catching dust and dirt, and then it is removable so that you can blow air on things with a simple switch on the side. There is a small hose extension for focused air flow.

CORD
This charges with a USB /micro USB cord.

VACUUM BRUSHES
This comes with two brushes. One fits on the extension bar and the other fits in the top of the clear blue catcher container.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
VACUUM
Honestly it is okay as a vacuum, but I have other vacuums that are cordless that I prefer. The only thing that this excels at for me is keyboard and other very fine cleaning. I don't find the suction as great as I would like and the blowing air from the vents is so heavy it blows things around as I move with the vacuum.

AIR BLOWING
For blowing, that is another story. This little gem is fabulous. I take the blue top off and put the switch at the blowing and it empties out my sewing machine bobbin area beautifully. It also blows out keyboard and other areas of the laptop that need cleaning.

CHARGES
I have used this since I got it for several weeks and it has not needed to be charged again. I only use it as needed, so it is probably going to stay charged for a while. It only took a little over and hour to charge when I got it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Nice to have as a little vacuum, this excels at blowing air. It is rechargeable so no need to buy any more cans of air that don't work or end up breaking. This is something I have wanted for a long time. I am thrilled to have it.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is fantastic. I absolutely love it. My husband is going to get one for his business too. He ain't touchin' mine! (grins)

text_fidelity_a:
Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I'm a software developer who works in a cubicle world with the heating system droning on above the ceiling (we're on the top floor of an office building - the HVAC is on the roof). These headphones provide an oasis of silence! The noise cancellation *seems* to be a cut above the others I've tried (Beats Studio at Target and a Sony set at Costco) although it's not really fair to compare as I didn't try the Bose under the same condition as the others (i.e. in a noisy store).

How good is it? The droning AC noise is completely gone. Voices I can still hear - until I play music. Even at low/moderate playback volume, voices are barely audible. People have to pat me on the back if they want my attention.

Comfort is excellent. I wear them on-and-off all day without problems. I imagine people with big ears might be less comfortable.

Power: the headphones use a single AAA battery. Keeping in mind that I maybe play music for 2-3 hours every day, the battery seems to last 2-3 weeks. As others have noted, these headphones will not work (i.e. play music) without power.

My one nitpick (and the reason I can't give it 5 stars) is the god-awful chord. It's some cheap plasticky material that I continually have to unravel by dangling the headphones by the plug end and letting the headphones rotate. It's really quite pathetic to put such cheap cr$p on $300 headphones - shame on Bose for not correcting this. Is it really going to affect your profitability so much you can't do something like the $20 Apple headphones that come with every iPhone (they're more rubberized and don't seem to get raveled).

Update for iPhone/iPad/iPod users: with iOS 7, Apple introduced a new way to invoke Siri (Apple's voice assistant) - instead of holding down the home button (or center button on the headphones) until you hear the Siri confirmation sound and then asking Siri your question and then waiting for Siri to accept your input, with iOS 7, you can keep the button pressed until you're finished talking - and avoid the delay Siri normally waits to know you're done with talking. It's a very useful feature.....and, it doesn't work with the Bose inline chord button :-( Not really Bose's fault, I guess, but I thought it worth mentioning.
text_fidelity_b: Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a: Polaroid Originals OneStep 2 VF - Summer Blue (9016) My youngest son graduated from high school this past weekend. I wanted him to be able to capture memories. Kids today use their cameras, but never go on to print out the photos. Of course, I am from a generation where we use to print out photos and scrapbook or place them in a photobook. Instead kids today Instagram or Snapchat, simply posting a memory that will be gone if those platforms crash. So, I instead am trying to get my son to capture some moments on film. The Polaroid Original One Step 2 provided gives him that option. Simply point and shoot. Instant fun, instant prints, instant memories captured.  I remember begging for a Polaroid when I was younger.  My parents said that they were expensive, and it seemed to take some time before “Santa” gave me one. I simply ordered mine on Amazon. While some would say that the film is kind of expensive, 8 pics for about $18.00 which equals a little over $2 a photo, it is FUN and the exciting thing is now you can get black & white film. text_fidelity_a: SABRENT USB 3.0 Tool Free Enclosure for 2.5” and 3.5” Internal SATA Hard Drives (EC-KSL3) I was all set to return this because it would not recognize my Seagate 4TB SSHD. In disk management it showed up as GPT protective partition. After googling, I found that the only way to get past this was to use Diskpart and Clean the drive--that meant wiping out everything on the drive. Since I had already cloned it, I went ahead and used the Clean command and wiped it out. Still couldn't do anything with the drive in disk management. So using Diskpart again, I used the command, Create Partition Primary. At this point, Diskpart couldn't do anything else. It would not create a volume to format, so I had to use Disk Management to create the volume and format it to exFat. I should state that the drive was recognized by my computer internally when it was connected to a Sata port, but once it was put into the Sabrent, it's drive information was changed and made unusable until I performed the procedure above. Not sure why this happened, maybe because it's a SSHD, but I kinda doubt it since I had no problems with the drive when connected to a Sata Port.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT USB 3.0 Tool Free Enclosure for 2.5” and 3.5” Internal SATA Hard Drives (EC-KSL3)

text_fidelity_a:
Skullcandy Hesh ANC Wireless Over-Ear Noise Cancelling Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone and Android with Microphone / 22 Hour Battery Life / Best for Music, School, Workouts, Travel, and Gaming - White I have worked with numerous pairs of active noise canceling (ANC phones) and I’ve seen a wide variation in sound profiles, features, and the quality of the ANC function. Some are better than others. I was a bit skeptical of these because of the price; most of the ANC phones I have used that were worth anything have a higher price tag. These are better than the price suggests.

Right out of the box, these headphones do not draw much attention to themselves. They’re not flashy and do not have any noticeable markings on them unless you’re looking for them. They are over-the-ear headphones which tend to be more comfortable than on-ear phones, and these have a snug fit without clamping down tightly. They adjust easily to fit almost any size head too. The padding on the cans is soft enough to not pinch, though after extended wear they do start to get a little warm.

Pairing and connection with my computer was a painless affair and these were ready very quickly after they were powered on.

The ANC function is far and away better than any other headphones I have worked with in this price range. They’re almost as aggressive as that of the Bose QC-15’s that I own, without that weird faux pressure sensation when the ANC is turned on. Even with the volume down low, these cancel out enough background noise to make them a serious contender. I have no complaints with the ANC.

The sound quality is very good, though not quite to my tastes. The bass is very strong – much stronger than I like personally, but not out of line with what has been trending in the last decade. Where Skullcandy got it right, though, is in how well they’ve implemented the bass enhancement. Even though the bass is very strong (enough to give me a headache at higher volumes), it does not distort or turn into just low-frequency noise. More importantly, the bass enhancement does not stomp on the midrange which is the usual casualty. The midrange is warm and fairly balanced. The highs are bright and clear without being piercing. The end result is a sound profile that sounds full and rich. So many headphones with enhanced bass I have used have killed the midrange which makes music sound hollow, or distort the bass so much as to make music sound like a low-fidelity render. These are refreshing in that regard.

Some headphones detect when you take them off and pause music or playback when you take them off. These do not.

These come in a carry pouch that offers little in the way of drop and crush protection but it does keep them clean and free of scuffs and scratches. Also included is an audio cable for wired use as well as a USB Type C cable for charging.

Overall, these are far and away better than the price would suggest. They are very comfortable to wear, they have a good sound profile (particularly if you like heavy bass) and the ANC function is better than average and competitive with much more expensive headphones. These are budget-friendly ANC headphones with higher-end performance.
text_fidelity_b: Skullcandy Hesh ANC Wireless Over-Ear Noise Cancelling Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone and Android with Microphone / 22 Hour Battery Life / Best for Music, School, Workouts, Travel, and Gaming - White

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS ZenDrive Silver 13mm External 8X DVD/ Burner Drive +/-RW with M-Disc Support, Compatible with both Mac & Windows and Nero BackItUp for Android devices (USB 2.0 & Type-C cables included) Looking back at all the recordable data storage media formats that have fallen by the wayside over the years, I guess it's inevitable that writable CD/DVD will eventually go obsolete too.

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2 (32GB, Black) There are more than enough helpful reviews, product specs and Q&A, so I am going to focus on this tablet for folks who are upgrading from another Android tablet, and especially another Samsung. I'll say up front that the biggest reason [for me, anyway] is the extra screen real estate and resolution.

I had a small surprise in that mine did not come with Amazon apps pre-installed like they did on my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 (10.1-Inch, White) 2013 Model]] that it replaced. Locating the App Store application so I could install all of the applications that I have purchased was a bit of a hassle, but I finally got that resolved. Like my older Samsung tablet this one is a little less than spectacular when it comes to streaming music to a speaker via bluetooth. I do not know why Samsung cannot get it right on tablets because I have never experienced any issues streaming on my Note II and Note 3 phones.

Another issue of which you need to be aware is this tablet is thin and flexible. I knew that in advance and purchased a [[ASIN:B00KCDBD2E Samsung Galaxy Note Pro 12.2-inch Case Cover]], which in my opinion is one of the better cases for this tablet. The hard shell part of the case into which you insert the tablet provides a rigid casing that allows zero flex. No matter which case you ultimately select I strongly recommend that you get one.

You may have issues with some apps if you opt to install an SD card to expand your storage, or if you are moving an SD card from another tablet to this one. The KitKat version of the operating system will not write to SD cards under certain conditions. There is a free fix called SD KitKat Fixer by JRummy Apps that you can get from the Play Store. I highly recommend it. As a side note, I had no issues with this SD card: [[ASIN:B00N2ROG9O PNY Turbo Performance 64GB High Speed MicroSDXC Class 10 UHS-1]]. It is an inexpensive way to max out your memory. I have heard that this tablet will work with 128GB cards, but I have not tested any so cannot say for sure.

If you are accustomed to Samsung's user interface you will feel right at home. For me, after the little challenges I mentioned above I was fully up and operational on this tablet in a few hours. A lot of that time was reinstalling purchased apps from Amazon and the Play Store, tweaking my settings so that they mirrored those on my Tab 10.1 (which are identical to my Note 3 phone), and this feels as comfortable as an old shoe. A much larger old shoe to be sure, and it's incredible how much extra screen space you get going from 10.1 to 12.2.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2 (32GB, Black)

However since it has no internal power source, it uses the power of the battery you are testing to give you a reading. This requires a power drain on the battery you are testing, which will ALWAYS give you inaccurate results. If you take a very small battery, such as a 1.5 V watch battery that is 1/3 depleted, this may be as mush as 30% off on the low side. Example, I checked a 1.5 V watch batty and this showed 1.0 V. Using a high end, self powered volt meter, the battery shoed 1.4V. That is a huge difference.

So again, it will show you a dead battery, but so will dropping a battery on end on a hard surface, If it bounces its dead, if it thuds and does not bounce, its good. Work on all AA, AAA, C, D. batteries.

eufy security, SoloCam E40, Outdoor Security Camera, Advanced AI Person-Detection, Two-Way Audio, 2K Resolution, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Only, IP65 Weatherproof, No Monthly Fee I contacted Eufy after the battery died after 4 weeks. Took them 2 days to send me an autobot emailed response to which I responded that I wanted a live person to email me. Another 2 days, and a person asked me to send a screen shot of the battery settings. REALLY??? So I did that which my battery settings were for optimized battery life. Another 2 days and still no answer. There was an option on the bottom of their email to escalate the case to management if I was not happy with the response, and that they would get back to me within 24 hours. So I clicked it, and explained how I was not getting a response. But guess what? I never got a response. So five days later, I decided to return this because I'm still in the return window. Maybe I had a defective unit. We have had a very mild winter, so I cannot imagine that the weather would make a supposed four-month battery charge only last for four weeks. Plus, there isn't much motion going on to drain the battery either. Sometimes, 3 or 4 days go by with no motion. The most number of times it has detected motion in one day is four times. So it's not like the battery is getting drained from the camera being triggered 10 times a day. I'm going to try one more time, and watch the battery life to see how quickly it drains before the return window closes.

**** Update **** The replacement camera will have a battery life of approximately 6 or 7 weeks, judging by the amount of battery used thus far. Since the return window is just 4 weeks, I have returned this camera again and will not try another one. 6-7 weeks battery life is better than 4 weeks, for sure. But still disappointing because Eufy advertises a 4 month battery life. I would have been willing to try to Eufy 2 Pro that has a 365-day battery life (figuring it probably really only has a 6 month battery life). But this would mean purchasing a home base. Also, the location of the camera does not get any direct sunlight, so even a solar panel would not have helped. If you are looking for just one camera that is wireless, and you aren't interested in having to take it down every month or two for recharging, this is not the camera for you. Their customer support contacted me the day after I wrote my first review. (I couldn't get any support previously through their normal channels.)

text_fidelity_a:
My Zone Wireless Headphones I got these headphones because I tend to put the TV on much louder than is comfortable for my husband, and the price was quite affordable. (That is to say, cheap.) Unfortunately, the saying, "You get what you pay for," applies in spades to my experience with this product.

I could not get the headphones hooked up by myself, and my husband, who is an IT guy, had to fiddle with them on and off over several days. He finally had to buy an [[ASIN:B000068O51 adapter]] to get it to work with our TiVo and TV combination, but while he could use the earphones once hooked up with little static, this was not the case for me. I had lots of static problems.

Here are the instructions we figured out to make it work with a TiVo, as well as it can be made to work once it is hooked up:

1. Pick up the headphones and the remotes for the TV and TiVo.
2. Stand directly in front of the TV.
3. Turn on the transmitter for the headphones.
4. Turn on the remote headphones by spinning the volume control dial on one side of the headphones. You might hear or feel a click when you spin the dial. A red light on the headphones will come on when they are turned on.
5. Press the Reset button on the headphones.
6. Put your finger on the Scan button on the remote headphones so you will know where it is.
7. Put the headphones on.
8. Press the Scan button.
9. You should now hear the sound of the TV through the headphones.
10. If you do not hear the TV, press Scan again until you hear the TV through the headphones.
11. You control the volume in the headphones with the volume dial on the side of the headphones.
12. You should turn the TV volume all the way down (or very low) using the TV remote since the TV remote does not control the volume of the headphones.

I rate this product as follows:

Ease of installation: 1 star
Ease of Use: 4 stars
Effectiveness of Product: 4 stars for IT husband, 2 stars for me, average 3 stars

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra EASYGO Bluetooth Headset [Retail Packaging] As a general rule, I hate hands-free handsets.

I hate it when I begin speaking with someone, and I think they're agreeing with everything I say, and then it turns out they're actually talking to someone else using their dratted ear extension with the flashing blue light.

I hate the fact that my ears are the wrong size and shape for the majority of headsets.

I hate it when my untrained (clumsy) fingers hit the wrong part of the headset when I'm simply trying to stop it from falling to its death from a height of just over 5 feet, and I either redial the last number or hang up on the one person who hates being hung up on.

Plus, they're UGLY, and don't accessorise well with any wardrobe!!

HOWEVER,

I hate it even more when I have to pull over and park to take or make a call.

And I especially hate it if I DON'T pull over, and then get busted by the only policeman on the entire empty highway who has insomnia and a full book of blank tickets waiting to be filled in.

SO,

Hands free it shall be -
But ONLY when I'm driving.

That said, this device fits most of my basic needs, and throws in some convenient extras. The EASYGO Headset was indeed very easy to set up and even easier to use. Sound quality was good and the spoken connection status and audio volume adjuster are useful features.

The headset is also relatively small and stylish (as hands-free headsets go) without any flashing lights or buttons that attract unwanted attention (or cause an attack of photosensitive epilepsy, or signal the letters N-E-R-D in morse code.)

The most impressive feature of this headset has to be the long battery life, which is great because the miserly charger cord is so awkward to use that you don't want to have to use it more often than necessary. Besides, as I only use it in the car, it lasts me several trips, depending on how often and how long I prattle.

Admittedly it is more comfortable to use than I expected. The extra ear hook prevents suicidal leaps from ear to earth, and it doesn't weigh my head down on one side.

In summary, for a simple headset, it delivers.

Rated: 4.5 stars

Amanda Richards
January 19, 2011
text_fidelity_b: Jabra EASYGO Bluetooth Headset [Retail Packaging]

When it comes to the Type-C port, consumers now need to have a phd in electronics just to understand what works with what. There are just so many standards crammed into this reversible port that you need to really read the fine print to know whether it will work for your uses. What's worse is that once you throw these cables into a drawer, good luck finding the right one.

Type-C cables that come with your phone or phone charger will generally only be good for charging your phone, but not great for transferring data. This Type-C cable will carry up to 100w of power, meaning it will charge your phone or tablet at the highest speed it can support. When transferring data, this cable will allow you to copy files at the highest USB 3.1 speeds.

But more than that, this cable supports video signals so that it will be usable to connect your laptop or phone to a portable type-c monitor (assuming your devices support it).

Personally, I got this cable to work with a pair of NReal Air video glasses so that I have a backup to the cable included in the box. These cables work but are a little bit stiff.
text_fidelity_b: Aoybevty USB C to USB C 3.1/3.2 Cable 6FT, 10Gbps Data Transfer 100W Fast Charging 4K@60Hz Video Monitor Cable for Thunderbolt 4/3 Laptop Tablet Cell Phone USB Type C Electronics Devices

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung SSD 860 EVO 4TB 2.5 Inch SATA III Internal SSD (MZ-76E4T0B/AM) I have built systems with SSDs for the last several years and I have come to see where they have their strengths and weaknesses. Not all SSDs are the same, and some have distinct advantages over others though the gap is definitely narrowing. This is my first experience with Samsung’s SSDs, and so far it has been a very positive experience. It has given me no issues at all and has performed well.

I installed the drive in a Dell Inspiron laptop which was running Windows 8. On the SSD, I installed Linux instead. Installation was very smooth, it was quick and I had a working system up and running in no time. I have now been running the system constantly for over a week (no powering off or hibernating) and the drive has shown no signs of trouble.

I loaded up a virtual machine and ran it on top of the main installation. The VM and the host install both have performed admirably and have not suffered from any noticeable I/O lag. Running smartctl against the drive after the past week of testing, it has reported no errors and a very healthy drive across the board.

Aside from the speed advantages of an SSD over a platter-based drive, this drive is absolutely silent (no surprise there) and so far I have not had any heat issues. It has given me no indications of any trouble in operation and my system is running as smoothly as should be expected.

The one issue I have with this drive, and it’s not a performance or quality issue, is the pricing. It is a little more expensive than most, and so far I have not seen any real justification for it over the likes of Crucial, Kingston or other branded drives. There may be justifiable reasons that reveal themselves later (I do not know how long this drive will continue to work but it should literally last for several years, even under very heavy use), but for now it seems a tad expensive compared to competitors.

Operationally I cannot find fault with this drive. It works well, it’s fast and quiet (as should be expected) and so far I’ve not had heat issues with it. Utilities I have run against it have shown that the drive is very healthy and has reported no problems out of the box. This is a good drive that will serve well. Time will tell, though, if it is worth the slightly higher asking price.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung SSD 860 EVO 4TB 2.5 Inch SATA III Internal SSD (MZ-76E4T0B/AM)

But this little speaker wins it hands down for being so compact. I am looking forward to throwing this speaker into my bag and listening to it at work. I also loved this speaker as it allows me to use my shuffle, nano or classic (which the ihome only allows for the bottom insert to be used) whereas the x-mini uses the earphone port (more universal for the different ipod models).

I also like this speaker as it uses the universal USB port to charge the chargeable battery in the speakers. I hope these rechargeable batteries last a long time! I dont think they are replaceable looking at the build of the speaker.

For the price,this is a great little speaker and so easy to carry around. I just ordered two more for family members. I noticed the x-mini max is about to be released (two speakers) and ~$30 more expensive, but I think this one is so more fun!

Sudio N2 Pro True Wireless Bluetooth in-Ear Earbuds with ANC - Multipoint Connection, IPX4 Water Resistant, USB-C and Wireless Charging, Microphone, 30h Play Time with Charging Case (Blue) I’ve used the Sudio N2 Pro Earbuds for about a month, and I like them. I typically wear them for about 2-3 hours a day while working at my desk, and I have two major pros and three major cons I’ve noticed during the last month.

PROS:
🎵 The earbuds are super comfortable! I have multiple inner ear piercings in both ears (rook, daith, tragus) and a LOT of earbuds hurt after about thirty minutes. I can wear the Sudio N2s for several hours at a time. Small, medium, and large silicone tips are included so you can get a good fit depending on your ears. Sometimes I walk around my house and do chores with these in, they haven’t fallen out once.

🎵 For earbuds, the ANC is good! I can actually notice a difference with the ANC on and off; with some earbuds that claim to have noise cancelling, there’s really no difference. The ANC on the Sudio N2s blocks out when the television is playing in the next room, and even muffles the sound of the heater right under my desk.

CONS:
🎵 Battery life is not great. With ANC on, I get 4 hours, maaaaybe 4.5 if I’m lucky. I put the case on my charging pad every other day, it seems. The case supports wireless charging, which is a positive, or via USB-C. I’ve noticed the earbuds don’t always turn off when put in the case and the lid is closed, which undoubtedly contributes to the faster battery drain.

🎵 The earbuds support Multipoint connection, or connecting to multiple devices, but I can only get them to connect to my Mac. No matter what I try, they will not connect to my phone (Samsung Note 20 Ultra). I tried every suggestion in the online manual, but I can’t even get the earbuds to factory reset.

🎵 The touch controls are VERY sensitive. I have to make sure I don’t have any video tabs open when I put them in, or the video starts blasting in my ear. The only audible cue I noticed was to turn ANC on, and that is “Noise Cancelling.” A beep indicates turning it off, and beeps are used for all other cues. I don’t know what does what, I just wish I could turn them off.

Although the cons slightly outweigh the pros, I still use the Sudio N2s every day. The comfort is a huge factor for me. I’ve tried probably 8 pairs of earbuds in the last year, and this is the only pair I can wear for more than an hour at a time.
text_fidelity_b: Sudio N2 Pro True Wireless Bluetooth in-Ear Earbuds with ANC - Multipoint Connection, IPX4 Water Resistant, USB-C and Wireless Charging, Microphone, 30h Play Time with Charging Case (Blue)

Belkin 6-Outlet Surge Protector with 3-Foot Cord (Plus An Extra 6-Foot Extension Cord) I'm confused. I thought when I got this surge suppressor that the extension cord was meant to be used with it so you'd have a total of nine feet of cord if needed. Apparently, the extension cord doesn't actually fit the surge suppressor; the extension cord has three two-prong receptacles that you could plug, say, lamps and the like into, but you cannot plug the surge suppressor itself into it. The extension cord is clearly marked as being for two-wire polarized, as opposed to three-prong grounded, appliances. So that's more than a little misleading.

The surge suppressor looks heavy-duty, but you are cautioned in the packaging literature that it's not to be used with "sensitive equipment" like everything we use surge suppressors for: computers, TV, etc. You can't use it with things involving water, either, like aquariums. So what would I use it for? A blow dryer? I think not. To make it even worse, you are told to cover the receptacles on the extension cord if they are not in use. There are little plastic sliders that you're supposed to use for this purpose. But one of the sliders on the extension cord I received won't stay closed. China-cheap.

Belkin has some good products, but this one doesn't impress me very much. And the whole thing is packaged in one of those awful clamshells that you risk hurting yourself on when you take the scissors to it.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin 6-Outlet Surge Protector with 3-Foot Cord (Plus An Extra 6-Foot Extension Cord)

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory Recording my listening experience with the Sennheiser HD 598 which I bought after breaking my pair of HE-400 headphones. I own Grado Labs SR80, BModed Fostex T50, Sennheiser HD-600, Hifiman HE-500.

Hour 1:
Pro: Looks good for plastic and reasonably comfortable.
Con: heavy handed, muddy, base reminds me of a one-note subwoofer, and the signature reminds me of a cheap pair of Skullcandy headphones. You could get better sound from a pair of Beat headphones. I am feeling ripped off and don't recall the last time listening to music made me MAD!
One word: Garbage!

Hour 10:
The headphones have opened up some. Vocals feel recessed. Bass still feels one dimensional. Upgraded rating from one to two stars.

Hour 15:
I am baffled by the positive reviews of this product. Yes, headphones and their sound signatures are very much a personal preference, but these are so grossly bad that I can only assume my ears are damaged or the headphones are defective. Returning them to Amazon.

text_fidelity_a:
Arteck Wireless Solar Keyboard Full Size Solar Recharging Keyboard for Computer/Desktop/PC/Laptop/Surface/Smart TV and Windows 10/8 / 7 / Vista/XP Built in Rechargeable Battery I selected this keyboard after doing a bit of research. I already have a solar keyboard (a Logitech) on my Windows system, and I needed a keyboard for my Linux system. I was a little hesitant to buy because I did not see any definitive information that it would work with Linux. I've had it several days, and I can say with some authority, it definitely works correctly under Linux.

The system in question is a Dell laptop running Peppermint Linux hosting a CentOS 8 VM. Most keyboards (with one notable exception) work on this system so I was hopeful it would work well, and it does. It behaves virtually identically to the Logitech keyboard and so far has given me no trouble.

Build-wise, this is a solid keyboard that should hold up to some abuse. It is sturdy and does not flex when I am typing. I like the fact that the dongle is held to the back of the keyboard magnetically so it can be transported with less concern of being misplaced when not in use.

One of the major issues I have with keyboards is that I have the hands of a gorilla and I frequently run into issues with hitting multiple keys at the same time, particularly with flat keyboards like this one. The keys are slightly bigger than average with this one, though, and hitting muliple keys simultaneously is less of a problem. This was an unexpected and welcome surprise.

Aesthetically, I love the feel of this keyboard. Most of the keys are concave and feel pleasant to the touch. Oddly, a good number of the keys on the bottom row are actually convex. While this is no issue at all, I do find it puzzling.

It is priced competitively against the Logitech too.

If I could change anything I would include some kind of indicator of how much charge this keyboard has at any given time. So far I have not run out of power, but eventually I expect to have a situation where there has not been enough light to keep it at a full charge and it would be good to know how much power it has retained.

I'm pleased with this keyboard. It works well under Linux and I don't need to replace batteries or plug it in. I really can't ask for much more than that.
text_fidelity_b: Arteck Wireless Solar Keyboard Full Size Solar Recharging Keyboard for Computer/Desktop/PC/Laptop/Surface/Smart TV and Windows 10/8 / 7 / Vista/XP Built in Rechargeable Battery

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic SC-HTB15 Home Theater System (2011 Model) You know how, with some movies, you can't hear the dialog for all the sound effects? This normalizes (or levels) the sound, so you can. It provides a better-than theater quality sound experience, for those of us who like to hear the dialog, experience the rich tones of the score, and not go deaf. Oh, it can get mighty loud if you want too. User's choice. It delivers a grand sound experience at any setting.

The setup is the "impress your kids" kind. It's easy, but it looks hard. You will need a Phillips head screwdriver, an [[ASIN:B003L1ZYYM AmazonBasics High-Speed HDMI Cable (6.5 Feet/2.0 Meters) - Supports Ethernet, 3D, and Audio Return [Newest Standard]]] and possibly (unless you have HDMI ARC) an [[ASIN:B001TH7GSW AmazonBasics Digital Optical Audio Toslink Cable, 6 Feet]]. Get them on Amazon. Most places charge a lot more for these. My TV didn't specifically state it was HDMI ARC (Audio Return Channel) but it worked anyway. I'm connected via an HDMI switcher, no problem. I just have the switch put out to the sound system, then the sound system put out to the TV. Everything is labelled and color coded, and it just couldn't be any easier. The only "gotcha" is make certain you're on the right input setting. Sometimes it wants TV instead of one of the HDMI ports.

It comes with a remote, in case your remote boat isn't already overflowing.

This is pretty much the top of the line. It's beautiful. It delivers awesome sound. It's perfect. I'm using my TV instead of my stereo to listen to music, because the sound quality of these speakers is that good. Oh, and you can turn the TV off and the speakers on, and the sound will still work.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic SC-HTB15 Home Theater System (2011 Model)

MEE audio M6 X1 Wired In-Ear Sports Headphones with Microphone and Remote – Sweatproof Secure Fit Earphones for Running, Jogging, and Gym Workouts (Black) (EP-X1-GYBK) Even pre break-in, these sounded great: probably the best headphones under $20 I've found. After break-in, these MEE buds were sounding like something that cost 4-5 times as much with a nice, even frequency response that favors bass only slightly. I find them comparable to $60-$80 Sennheisers, my previous favorites (which superseded Sony and Koss buds that I also liked). These MEE buds came with 3 sets (S, M, and L) of your typical soft rubber earpieces as well as 2 sets of the interesting multi-tiered earpieces shown in the photos and a pretty standard cloth case. Between the various earpiece options, it's unlikely anyone will have an issue finding a good fit.

The cord is about 1 m long, which suits my purposes. I like the over-the-ear wire bits, too, as they prevent tugs on the cord from dislodging them. They might be awkward with some kinds of glasses, but my straight-earpiece sunglasses fit over them fine. They can be bent to hang down more like normal earbuds if desired, though.

I'll be checking out more MEE products now, seeing what a great value these were. I still favor AKG and Beyerdynamic at the high end, but for my biking/hiking/running/workout listening needs, I'll probably be coming back to MEE.
text_fidelity_b: MEE audio M6 X1 Wired In-Ear Sports Headphones with Microphone and Remote – Sweatproof Secure Fit Earphones for Running, Jogging, and Gym Workouts (Black) (EP-X1-GYBK)

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser HD 598 SR Open-Back Headphone "Discontinued by manufacturer" My household has a variety of headphone fans in it. The headphone level of appreciation varies from "I will listen to anything as long as it works" to "I don't hear that sound exactly as I want to, so these are no good". I am in the middle. I love a good headphone, but I am not addicted to analyze every single sound and micro focus on them. What I am looking for is a headphone which has good sound separation, realistic presentation, but not too much distortion or muffled sound.

My purpose for wanting headphones with a cord was duo-fold. I want a set of headphones to listen to my desktop or laptop in my living room while people are watching TV, and I also wanted a set of headphones for my tablet so I could watch video demonstrations for my spinning wheel, knitting, and other crafts in the living room while the rest of the family is watching TV and I need to a quick refresher on a project I am working on.

WHAT ARE THESE HEADPHONES LIKE?
In the box (a nice box with excellent protection for the headphones), there is a set of headphones, two cords, and an extra plug adapter. The headphones themselves are lightweight for what they are. They are marked R and L so that you will put them on the correctly way easily. The ear cushions are a velveteen fabric which a lightweight foam inside. The cord jack is on the left ear phone. The top of the headphones has a soft leatherette foam which is very soft and easily squished.

The long cord measures about 118 inches. It comes with a large jack for stereos on one end and the smaller jack which fits into the headphones. The additional adapter for the smaller jack which fits into phones and tablets. The smaller cord measures approximately 48 inches and has a phone answering. This one has a smaller jack for phones and tablets.

HOW DO THESE HEADPHONES FIT?
I found that these headphones fit everyone in the family very nicely. Even my headphone fanatic liked them although he said his phones were a little nicer but not much.

HOW DO THESE HEADPHONES PERFORM?
I really like these. I have tried them with music, videos, movies, and other sounds from classes to classical. I find them to be realistic and high quality. It feels like I am in the room with the sounds - hearing squeaking of chairs, or fingers on strings - but yet it feels more natural than sound proof headphones. I can still hear what is going on around me, so if really loud music is happening in the room, these are not overly helpful, but that does not happen here so I am fine with them.

I found the sound clarity to be nice. No muffled sounds or blurry sound with these that I have noticed thus far. The bass is nice- not too much, but not overwhelming either. Of course, that depends on the recording I am listening to. There are no controls on the headphones.

Due to the cushioning these are comfortable. If I have a tender head (such as headache type day) they tend to hit a sensitive area of my head so I can not wear them as long as I would like, but most of the time, I can wear them comfortably for extended periods of time. It is nice because I can hear what is going on in the room around me if I need to so it does not block me from having to pay attention to things around me when necessary.

HOW DO THESE WORK WITH A TABLET?
I found these to work very well with my tablet. Using them for visual lessons at my spinning wheel and knitting chair is perfect- just what I wanted. I can hear what I need and not feel closed in with them on either.

CAN OTHER PEOPLE HEAR THEM IN A QUIET ROOM?
That is the one drawback about these headphones- if you are in a library, or quiet room, people around you will be able to hear what you are listening to unless it is very low volume and then you will have to strain to hear.

HOW DO THEY WORK WITH A PHONE?
I have not used them with my phone yet so have not had the chance to use the phone features. I tend to use my tablet most of the time. I will update when I have experience in that area to add.

OTHER COMMENTS
My son who is the headphone fanatic was even impressed with these headphones. He has several top line headphones (including Turtle Beach) and said that he was very impressed by the definition of sound, balanced bass and treble and clarity of these headphones. From him that is a compliment. He is rather stingy with glowing comments on most things electronic.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For the price of these headphones, this is a really nice set. Sound is clear, balanced, and realistic. The headphones are comfortable and well cushioned, making them wearable for extended periods of time. Lots of great sound and detail, yet the ability to hear the room around make them practical for use in a multitasking situation. They work great with tablets, laptops, and desktop although I have not tested a lot with my phone yet, my son has and they work great.

RATING
FIVE stars for these headphones. I am very happy with them. I plan to test in the future for gaming and phone answering and will update at that time.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser HD 598 SR Open-Back Headphone "Discontinued by manufacturer"

ASUS N900 WiFi Router (RT-N66U) - Dual Band Gigabit Wireless Internet Router, 4 GB Ports, Gaming & Streaming, Easy Setup, Parental Control After searching review after review for a router with solid performance and features I ended up with the N66. I am not a networking professional but I can tell you there is an enormous difference between a good N900 router and an N300 router you may have gotten from your ISP. I would take any review that is not written by a professional with a grain of salt but here's my 2 cents.

I live in a densely populated area with 20+ Wi-Fi networks with decent strength AND I live in a brick building. I have 50 Mps/down from my ISP and with this router I am able maintain at least 50 Mps throughout my ~900 ft2 apartment with one exception, the back porch. Speeds dip to about 15 Mps on the back porch on both the 2.4 & 5 Ghz bands, as I understand it Wi-Fi doesn't get along with brick. There is a brick wall in between my the rest my house and and finally my router. Understandable.

The takeaway, if you need a fast router, I think you will be hard pressed to find a better one. I haven't even touched on USB support for printers, USB applications & external storage, VPN, iOS applications, etc.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS N900 WiFi Router (RT-N66U) - Dual Band Gigabit Wireless Internet Router, 4 GB Ports, Gaming & Streaming, Easy Setup, Parental Control

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Gear IconX (2018 Edition) SM-R140NZKAXAR Bluetooth Cord-free Fitness Earbuds, w/ On-board 4Gb MP3 Player (US Version with Warranty) - Black I’m NOT an audiophile, but I was blown away by the sound quality delivered by these SAMSUNG GEAR ICONX (2018 Edition) BLUETOOTH CORD-FREE FITNESS EARBUDS (w/On-board 4Gb MP3 Player; Gray (SM-R140NZAAXAR)). I like classical music, and the sound is so relaxing and immersive, I forget that I’m wearing earbuds. (It helps that these are totally without wires, of course.)

The earbuds are far and away the most comfortable that I’ve ever worn. You get three sizes of in-ear tips (S, M, L). There is NO sound leakage to speak of. The touch controls for music work fine, though it takes some practice to master the double- and triple-taps (sound tracks) and swipes (volume) so that you get consistent results. For me, it’s easiest to play an album or list at a set volume, without fussing with the controls.

I didn’t test the call-answering features or other features beyond playing music. The earbuds paired, without incident, with my iPad Pro and with my Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge. The charging case seems to need to be charged up to the green light for pairing to work.

A great feature is that you can copy music files to the earbuds. They have 4GB of built-in storage. This means you don’t have to stay within Bluetooth range of your mobile device to play music.

Three stars because I haven’t used the earbuds consistently for a full month. As much as I love these, I’m afraid that the left earbud will fail before long (as other reviewers have reported).

Already the left earbud has exhibited signs of NOT charging properly. With the case closed and plugged in (and with brand-new earbuds), the left charging light blinked red, which indicates “not charging”. I corrected the problem by opening the case and reseating the left earbud in the cradle, but of course I’m wondering whether there is a more serious problem that will surface soon.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Gear IconX (2018 Edition) SM-R140NZKAXAR Bluetooth Cord-free Fitness Earbuds, w/ On-board 4Gb MP3 Player (US Version with Warranty) - Black

I saw these and fell in love with the colors. Is the performance just as nice? Let's take a look.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
These are the most gorgeous mint green and neon violet color. The ear phones are quite small and sit on top of the ears. The top is padded, and so are the earphones.

CORD
The cord is about 55 inches long or so. The jack is the small type meaning 3.5.

CONTROLS
The controls are in the line. There is a plus and minus for sound level and a phone button for answering. You can forward and go backwards through song lists.

ADJUSTMENTS
This is where these shine. You can not only pull the earphones down to make them longer, but they also swivel from left to right to better accommodate the face and ear placement on the head.

FOLDING
There are two ways you can store these. You can fold them flat, by rotating the ear phones to be flat with the rest of the headset, or you can fold the earphones up into the headset making them have a smaller footprint.

COMFORT
These are VERY comfortable. I am amazed that I don't even know they are on.

NOISE CANCELING
I am amazed at how well these work to keep me focused on the lessons as I do them.

QUALITY
WOW. The quality of these is WAY better than I expected. The sound is clear with no muffling at all. I am very happy with how these have performed so far. Music is amazing and my foreign language lessons are also fantastic.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Not only are these GORGEOUS in color, but they work beautifully. For the price, they are amazing. They work well with my old desktop as well as my tablet and old MP3 player.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I am very happy with these. Honestly they shocked me at how nice they are for the price.

PHOTOS
I would take a photo, but honestly they look JUST LIKE the photo with this listing.

I’m also running it on an external fan pad on full speed, but the fans still insist on blowing at almost max speeds on games that could run on a potato. I fear that overheating damage is inevitable and imminent with this rig.

text_fidelity_a:
Harman Kardon Allure Voice-Activated Home Speaker with Alexa, Black As an avid fan of Alexa, I am delighted to have this Harman Kardon Alexa speaker. I've had my original Echo since the first week they released the initial invitation to buy and have since added a Dot and Alexa controlled thermostats, dining room lights, Fire TV sticks and plugs through out the house. This unit was meant to enhance the music sound quality from Alexa and expand our Alexa listening group and work with the living room television.

The speaker itself is considerably larger than my original Echo - wider and heavier. The lights on this are brighter as well - when playing music at night or listening to a book, you can leave the light on and it works as a night light. You can also turn the light off if you prefer. Setting this up takes a bit longer than my Echo or Dot - it's slower making the initial WiFi connection, but once you link to Amazon via the Alexa App, you're good to go. It connects via Bluetooth to both my LG V10 phone and my Samsung tablets without drama.

This unit is significantly louder at every volume setting than the original Echo and makes the Dot sound like she's whispering. I have this in our formal living room where we have 30 feet tall ceilings, grass cloth covered walls and an enormous open space - the room was designed for correct accoustics with my Grandmother's grand piano and music simply sounds beautiful in here. The Harman Kardon Alexa sits on a table where the piano used to be and the sound at volume 4 simply envelopes you no matter where you are in the room. Set the volume to 6 and I can hear my book or music two rooms away almost as if it's floating through the halls. The sound quality is excellent and playing Beethoven or opera or country music renders each instrument precisely from tiny flutes to cellos and twangy fiddles. I'm immensely pleased at the improvement from the Echo to this for just music.

The reason for the one star deduction is because I thought/expected the Harman Kardon to by fully, 100% integrated with Alexa. It is not. This unit cannot be linked to the Fire TV sticks, meaning that I cannot use it to verbally control the living room television. It cannot be linked to my Echo and Dot units. That means we can't include the Harman Kardon speaker in our multi room group so the same song/book can be heard throughout the house. We cannot do the Drop In skill where Alexa acts as an intercom system for multiple rooms. There are a couple of other skills this speaker isn't able to perform simply because it doesn't speak to the Amazon Alexa products. If they can correct this glaring deficiency, then this would be a five star product and one i would consider buying for the guest suite and master bedroom. As a stand alone Alexa unit, this is a top notch choice, but if you want to link to your existing Echo, you can't do so.
text_fidelity_b: Harman Kardon Allure Voice-Activated Home Speaker with Alexa, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa, 10.1" HD Display, 16 GB, Black - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I love everything else Amazon has ever done, so it breaks my heart to write this review. I've had a couple of iPads and they work great, but I find Apple's pricing and politics ridiculous, so I was excited to move away from them and go with an Amazon product. Sadly, the Fire HD is seriously inferior.

This device is SLOW. Every step of the setup process was painfully slow. Downloading, and even opening, apps is slow. I have my OLD iPad sitting right next to the Fire HD performing the same functions on the same WiFi connection and the Fire takes 4 times as long to do anything.

The WiFi connectivity is not great. Again, I have my old iPad 3 sitting right next to this device, and the Fire HD keeps losing the network connection or dropping down to 1-2 bars, while the iPad is streaming and loading everything with lightning speed. Funny thing is, I have a Fire TV Stick running in the same room, and it has a wonderfully reliable, super-fast connection!

The touch screen is also sometimes not very responsive - I will have to tap some things 4-5 times before they trigger.

Most of the apps I was looking for are available in the Amazon App Store. However, these are buggy versions that appear to have been thrown together without the care that the developers have put into their iOs versions.

Possibly the worst part of all is the battery life. We are supposed to get 8 hours of usage.... I get about 4, even with the screen set as dim as possible. It also completely discharges on standby (with NO USE) within 2 days, even with the setting enabled to turn off WiFi when the device is on standby.

I do love the integration with the Amazon ecosystem. I hope someday Amazon will make the necessary improvements and I can give their tablets another chance. But for now, I will be returning this device with a heavy heart. :(
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa, 10.1" HD Display, 16 GB, Black - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
REETEC Wireless Bluetooth Headphones Over-Ear - [40 Hrs Playing Time, Soft Protein Earpads] Foldable HiFi Stereo Wireless Headphones with Microphone, Deep Bass Headset for Phone, PC, iPad - Rose Gold I've owned many wireless headphones, so this isn't my first rodeo. I wanted something separate to leave paired with my work computer. Earbuds aren't comfortable for me to wear for long periods of time so over-the-ear style is important. I have to admit, I like these more than I expected to. The ear pads are soft and slow to reclaim their shape like memory foam- this makes them extremely comfortable to wear so I don't mind keeping them on for a good portion of my workday. It also has a rubberized cover for the charging port and 3.5mm jack, which is surprisingly nice to find on a headset in this price range!
The sound quality is about on par with what I expected for this price range- that is, it is very good. Not blow-your-mind-amazing like sets that sell for hundreds, but as good if not better than others in this price range. What I didn't like, however, is the microphone quality. Yes, it has a mic, but I'd like to pretend it doesn't. The mic is on the headset by my ears and doesn't seem to be directed towards my mouth. This makes my voice sound distant and muffled, with ambient background noise sometimes on the same level or louder than my voice is. For calls I'd rather use a different headset, but that's OK. This ends up being used paired with my computer rather than my phone. It is pretty decent at passive noise isolation as well, reducing sound around you naturally. The only things I wish were better are the mic and perhaps a physical on/off switch rather than a button, but honestly this is pretty normal for headphones in this price range so I essentially got exactly what I expected.
EDIT:
I loved these so much, I ended up getting another on in another color for a family member. A great value for wireless headphones.
text_fidelity_b: REETEC Wireless Bluetooth Headphones Over-Ear - [40 Hrs Playing Time, Soft Protein Earpads] Foldable HiFi Stereo Wireless Headphones with Microphone, Deep Bass Headset for Phone, PC, iPad - Rose Gold

Jabra STONE Bluetooth Headset with Extreme-Noise Blocking (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Pros:

1. I liked it for its looks at first sight. One of the sleekest looking Bluetooth ear devices that I've ever seen.
2. Almost unnoticeable when nestled in tight, snuggling up to your ear
3. Nice convenient pod for charging and carrying around, looking like a cute little black egg

Cons:

1. Once you can get it to fit comfortably in your ear, it sounds wonderful. Unfortunately, it doesn't fit my ear and due to the placement of the invisible control buttons, every time I try to adjust it, I either disconnect the call or re-dial the last call.
2. It makes me do a LOT of redialling as it keeps slipping out of place.
3. Maybe I was doing something wrong but I couldn't get it to pair with my Blackberry or my iPod.
4. Does not keep the charge for the 8 hours as promised. It discharges very quickly (in a couple of hours, or so it felt) especially when compared to the length of time it takes to re-charge.
5. I couldn't use it on my left ear, which for me, wasn't quite right
6. The art of raising or lowering the volume by sliding a finger along the headset has thus far eluded me.

This device is one you'd buy for looks, but not for life.

Amanda Richards
October 25, 2010

text_fidelity_a:
Targus Versavu Rotating Keyboard Case and Stand for iPad 2, 3, and 4, Black (THZ17101US) This polyurethane Targus Versavu Keyboard Case is beautiful, with imitation-leather exterior and suede-like "soft touch" interior. A hard shell (also with imitation-leather exterior) holds the iPad firmly in place, yet the iPad can be easily removed. The shell is attached at the circular hole shown in the product photos; the hole allows the Apple logo to show through. The shell rotates (with the iPad inserted) a full 360 degrees, so that the stand and keyboard can be used when the iPad is oriented either horizontally or vertically.

The lightweight keyboard is about the same size as the keyboard on my Toshiba netbook. The flat, non-contoured keys are reasonably comfortable to use. The keyboard is surrounded by a raised edge, to prevent scratches or damage to the iPad screen. The keyboard must be charged independently (using the included USB cable, attached to your computer). The keyboard will give a low-charge warning at 15% power, and shut down at 10% power.

This case (with cutouts for buttons, switches, rear camera, and charger plug) fits my iPad 2 perfectly, and the Bluetooth keyboard connects with my iPad 2. I didn't expect it to work, because the iPad 2 is equipped with Bluetooth 2.1 + EDR technology, while the iPad 3 is equipped with Bluetooth 4.0 technology, and the product description says that the case requires an iPad 3. The case does NOT have an automatic iPad Wake/Sleep switch that operates when you open the cover; however, the keyboard puts itself to sleep after 10 minutes of inactivity.

I like this case and all of its features, but it's not the "perfect" iPad 2 case. It adds weight and bulk, and apparently--judging from other reviewers' statements--the manufacturer recommends against using the case for anything but display (no carrying the case around in a backpack, tote, or bag). Because the keyboard works well, I rate it at 3.5 stars, rounded up to 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Targus Versavu Rotating Keyboard Case and Stand for iPad 2, 3, and 4, Black (THZ17101US)

text_fidelity_a:
APC Power Strip with USB Charging Ports, Surge Protector P8U2, 2630 Joules, Flat Plug, 8 Outlets More electronics in the home means a need for more outlets. An ordinary extension cord will do the trick, but if you want something that looks nicer, has more functionality, and protects against power surges than one good option is the APC P11U2 APC Surge Arrest.

This surge protection device is great for those who need extra outlets for plugging in electronics and other things. It has eleven sockets plus 2 USB ports for a total of 13 places to plug things in and keep them running. An indicator light will tell you if there is an overload, which is highly possible when there are so any plugs. We don’t have this problem because we use this on our kid’s tech table. It allows them to plug in their cell phones, tablets, kindles, and other items- all which use minimal power- and get everything charged all at once without them fighting over limited outlet availability.

Each of the outlets on this surge protector has a safety closure, which is good for keeping out unwanted items. This can be useful if you have young children- wouldn’t want junior sticking a paper clip or other item inside one of the sockets. And a light glows to indicate that the surge protection is working as it should.

If I could change one thing about this, it would be the length of the cord. It would be better if it was just a little longer because it would be capable of reaching further. But other than that, this surge protector has worked just fine for my needs. It has ample space to plug in and charge all of our household electronics, keeping them ready for use and protecting against power spikes in the process.
text_fidelity_b: APC Power Strip with USB Charging Ports, Surge Protector P8U2, 2630 Joules, Flat Plug, 8 Outlets

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Basics SDHC Class 4 16GB Secure Digital Card the plus to this card is obvious--it has a large capacity.  The con is that it is a little slow in picture-taking.  Depending on what you're looking for, you may be happy or dissatisfied. I used it in a Kodak flip-style camcorder/still picture taker and I liked the fact that I didn't have to worry about filling up the card.  I recorded at 720 and it did fine in the recording and in the downloading of the video--I really didn't notice any speed issues.  Picture-taking was a different story; there was a noticeable lag in taking still photos. I wouldn't dismiss this card for that reason, however, unless a difference of a second or so will matter to you.  Most of my still picture taking on vacation is done with a larger point and shoot Canon IS, so the lag time with the little camera didn't matter much to me as I either used it mostly for video as mentioned or took stills of landscape or posed photos.  To be honest, I prefer not to use such a large capacity card for photos anyway as I have a fear of something going wrong with the card and losing hundreds of photos as opposed to a few videos.  So I'm happy to keep this in the little compact video camera and snap the occasional slow photo. I wouldn't put it in my Canon for the above reason and also because the photos I take with that I'd be more concerned about the sluggish picture-taking.  Be selective about how you use it, and I think you'll be more than satisfied
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics SDHC Class 4 16GB Secure Digital Card

This caused a lot of problems and I was constantly transferring my images to an external HDD and it was extremely inconvenient.

I decided to purchase this USB flash drive. It was low cost for such a large amount of space. Best decision I ever made!
I have had this in my laptop for the last 2 months and it has not fallen out or gotten damaged. I carry my laptop everywhere with me.
Data transfers are very fast. With less than 50 picutures, it's basically instant and I often feel the need to check and make sure the files actually transferred because it happens so quickly, I don't even get a "Transferring files" window. I have never had a failed transfer.

If you are using it in a mac, you will need to reformat it to ExFAT. It will work out of the box, but will not accept large folders or files until it is reformatted.

The only issue I've ever had is if my computer falls asleep, the drive will sometimes disconnect, but that is due to the settings on my computer and not the drive. A simple unplug-replug reconnects it.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices Got this Logitech Bluetooth adapter after a while and a bit of researching...

I wanted to connect my iPhone and iPad to my receiver in my living room so I could broadcast music throughout my house (I have speaker located in different rooms)
So I decided it came down to three options.

1. [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492-P Bluetooth Music Receiver]]
2. [[ASIN:B004VM1T5S Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices (980-000540)]]
3. [[ASIN:B0015YJOK2 Apple Airport Express MB321LL/A [NEWEST VERSION]]]

______________

Belkin

I got the Belkin Bluetooth Receiver [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492-P Bluetooth Music Receiver]] but I had complaints about range. Even though there is a fix (which requires opening it up and removing a metal piece which other reviewers have said is just added to add some weight)the range with the fix still is not up to par. The Sound quality was below par as well.

__________________
Apple Airport Express

The Apple Airport Express is unique in solving my problem as it has one major advantage... It uses the wireless network in my home to stream music to my receiver (not Bluetooth). Awesome idea and I actually ordered one. This way I could be way out of Bluetooth range (i.e. my backyard)and still control music through my iPhone or iPad through the wireless network.
The only problem with this setup (which in the end I refused to deal with) is that you can only use your iPhone or iPad as a REMOTE to control iTunes on a computer. Meaning that you need to have a computer on with the appropriate songs on at all times if you want to listen to music. Being that we have laptops only and there is no consistent computer in the house, let alone "on", and connected to the wireless network.
This could not work for me.
Second problem with this system is that you can only play iTunes. No Pandora or other music venues such as youtube etc.
And to top it all off this Apple Airport express cost $99!!(plus the use of a computer full time)

_______________________
Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices

This is very similar to the Belkin but it literally took 2 minutes to hook up and the range that I tested so far is incredible. That being said it is using Bluetooth not Wireless Network so don't expect total wireless connectivity. The Sound quality is on par with the apple but I assume that will degrade with distance to the receiver. Other wise it is perfect.

In summation I am very happy with this product at this price. I would gladly pay $100-$200 for a system like the Apple Airport express that could play all audio from my iPhone or iPad directly and didn't require me to only use my iPhone as a remote for a computer that can only play iTunes on the network.... Until a reasonable system comes out like that I think this product will do the job nicely.

Or if your so inclined you can quickly rack up a few thousand dollars setting up a Sonos System[[ASIN:B005441AJC Sonos Play:3 All-In-One Wireless Music Player With 3 Integrated Speakers (Black, NEW)]]
But My house is already wired with speakers and such and I don't feel it is worth the investment.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices

text_fidelity_a:
C2G/Cables to Go Audio Unlimited Premium Indoor/Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker, Black (SPK-131U) I was very excited to have a large speaker with bluetooth capability for my Iphone to use outside by the pool. This speaker was a total dissapointment on all levels. Or maybe I just received a lemon.

I thoroughly read the instruction manual - twice - to be certain I was doing everything correctly. When I was finally able to get the bluetooth to work (after having to hold down the button on the speaker until the blue light flashed multiple times, which let me know it was activated), it did work from various locations in my yard without any failures. However, as soon as I would turn off the speaker or my Iphone - I would need to re-initialize the bluetooth as if I were logging in for the very first time. The speaker failed to remember by device and so I'd begin the pressing down of the button, blue lights flashing procedure all over again. Every single time.

So I thought I'd contact the manufacturer/vendor to see if there was anything beyond their "trouble shooting" section of the manual that I might be neglecting. I looked everywhere - the box, the manual, the speaker, everywhere - no contact information whatsoever. Not an email address, phone number, snail mail or Facebook/Twitter address to be found. You buy it - you're stuck with it. The only saving grace is Amazon if you need to return it within the acceptable time frame. But what do you do if you have a problem 6 months down the line?

I installed the batteries, tried out the a/c adapter cord, and even used the 3.5 speaker cable to attach my Iphone and by-pass the bluetooth completely. I just wanted to make sure all of these items would work. But the person who designed this unit must have been having a wonderful time when they decided that in order to plug in anything at all, you need to open the battery compartment door in order to get to the connectors. This is insane and is in no way convenient. To constantly have to remove a door, or have cords hanging needlessly is ridiculous.

The sound quality is acceptable but at the price they're selling it for, you could do far better finding a speaker that has much more to offer. And if you're looking for customer service - keep looking cause it isn't here.
text_fidelity_b: C2G/Cables to Go Audio Unlimited Premium Indoor/Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker, Black (SPK-131U)

I downloaded a 3rd party migration/cloning software and that didnt work either. I tried nearly everything I could for 1.5 days! I even tried backing up/restoring manually and then repairing. Nothing worked. It was a complete waste of time. I didnt even learn anything in the process other than learning that I should go with a company that has a readily available comprehensive solution that doesn't needlessly waste your valuable time. 1.5 days down the drain.

So I ended up migrating my Samsung 1tb NVME to a new Samsung 2tb NVME and it couldnt have been any easier. < 15 minutes, very quick! I previously, migrated from a corsair SSD to Samsung 1tb NVME (when i couldnt get another SSD to migrate properly), and that was flawless as well. Why didnt I initially go with the Samsung 2tb instead of WD? Press had positive news about it. I am not a fanboy so I like to try different solutions. That was a mistake. What's apparent to me after this experience is that Samsung is better than all their competitors at providing a comprehensive package of the best hardware and software. The experience is FLAWLESS. I havent had any issues with any of their storage solutions to date.

Disclosure, I bought and paid for everything myself and I still own HDs/SSDs/MicroSds by WD (only old HDs), Sandisk (microsds, ssds), Seagate (HD), Samsung (SSDs, Micro SDs and NVMEs).

Update May 7, 2021

Still works as good as when I installed a month ago. No issues. Lightning fast.
